mechanism_narrative: Positive quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity that increases corporate earnings visibility, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days through improved risk appetite and lower discount rates.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth rate is positive in the prior quarter but S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 5.0% (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates and reduces corporate leverage capacity, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 5.0% but S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE) and decline in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates deteriorating labor market conditions and weak consumer demand, triggering equity sell-offs that produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rising UNRATE and falling RSAFS occur but S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Stagflationary conditions (CPIAUCSL > 285.0 index and UNRATE > 5.0%) combine persistent inflation with weak labor markets, forcing central banks to prioritize price stability over growth and depressing equity valuations, yielding negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 285.0 and UNRATE > 5.0% but S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate revenue visibility, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through improved earnings expectations.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth is positive in the prior month but S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 100.0 (INDPRO) indicates contraction in manufacturing output and services, reducing corporate capacity utilization and profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100.0 but S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) combined with rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive monetary policy response to inflation in a weak economy, increasing recession risk and depressing equity valuations for negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 5.0% and FEDFUNDS rising but S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Housing boom conditions (HOUST > 1700.0) combined with strong retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer spending and construction activity, driving economic expansion that produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1700.0 but S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.
